event: Smith and publicist Jonathan Hay start record label SMH Records (per Rolling Stone).
notes: Backstory only. Hay is a private individual; describe by role if used.

event: Reality competition 'One Shot', bankrolled by Smith with Smith as a judge, premieres on BET (per Rolling Stone).
notes: Backstory.

event: Smith's song 'You're My Kind of Beautiful' is in its 12th week on adult-contemporary radio charts (Billboard peak No. 35) (per Rolling Stone).
notes: Status-quo scene: a real
column7: modest music career before the scheme.

event: Indictment alleges Smith emails CC-1 to create bot accounts: 'Make up names and addresses'.
notes: Indictment ¶11(c) p.6.

event: Indictment alleges Smith emails himself the math: 52 cloud accounts x 20 bots = 1,040 bot accounts; ~636 songs/day each; ~661,440 streams/day; est. $3,307.20/day, $99,216/month, $1,207,128/year.
notes: Indictment ¶14 pp.7-8. Thumbnail/cold-open document. Not in the Superseding Information he pleaded to.

event: Distribution Company-1 tells Smith a song 'fit the criteria that is usually linked to store end streaming abuse'; Smith: 'I acknowledge what you wrote and I ask that you still release it. We have no intentions of committing streaming fraud.'
notes: Overt act (c) in the Superseding Information he pleaded guilty to (p.2); also indictment ¶27. Distribution Company-1 is unnamed - do not identify.

event: Distribution Company-1 reports 'multiple reports of streaming abuse from different stores' and plans to remove Smith's releases; Smith replies 'This is absolutely wrong and crazy! ... There is absolutely no fraud going on whatsoever! How can I appeal this?'
notes: Information overt act (c) p.2; indictment ¶27 p.13.

event: Indictment alleges Smith emails two co-conspirators: 'we need a TON of content with small amounts of Streams.'
notes: Indictment ¶15(d)(i) p.9.

event: Indictment alleges Smith reports hundreds of thousands of streams of AI music; CC-4 replies 'we've proved the model works.' (CC-4 had called it 'proof of concept'.)
notes: Indictment ¶19 p.10. TURN: AI removes the song shortage.

event: Indictment alleges Smith emails: 'We need to get a TON of songs fast to make this work around the anti fraud policies these guys are all using now.'
notes: Indictment ¶15(d)(ii) p.9.

event: Indictment alleges Smith and CC-3 sign a 'Master Services Agreement': 1,000-10,000 songs/month; Smith owns the IP and supplies song/artist names; pays greater of $2,000 or 15% of streaming revenue from the AI songs.
notes: Indictment ¶22 pp.10-11. CC-3 = 'Chief Executive Officer of an AI music company'; uncharged; do not name.

event: Streaming Platform-1 tells Smith's distributor it believes he engaged in streaming fraud; Smith denies to the distributor ('I have done NOTHING...') and writes to the platform ('You have slandered me to my distributors...').
notes: Information overt acts (d)-(e) p.3; indictment ¶¶28-29. Platform unnamed - do not identify.

event: Indictment alleges CC-3 emails Smith: 'this is not 'music,' it's 'instant music' ;)'.
notes: Indictment ¶20 p.10.

event: Indictment alleges Smith emails: 'I can't run the bots without content... If we get too many streams on one song it comes down.'
notes: Indictment ¶15(d)(iii) p.9.

event: Indictment alleges Smith reports 'We are at 88 million TOTAL STREAMS so far!!!', ~$110,000/month, CC-3 and CC-4 each receiving 10%, and asks for another 10,000 AI songs to 'spread this out more'.
notes: Indictment ¶21 p.10.

event: Indictment alleges CC-3 emails: 'Song quality is 10x-20x better now, and we also have vocal generation capabilities.'
notes: Indictment ¶24 p.12.

event: Indictment alleges Smith moves $1.3 million of royalties through an 'SMH Entertainment' account to a Manhattan debit-card service to fund bot accounts under fake employee names.
notes: Indictment ¶11(e) pp.6-7; basis of the dropped money-laundering count.

event: Indictment alleges Smith falsely represents to Distribution Company-2 that he would not engage in fraudulent streaming.
notes: Indictment ¶8 pp.4-5.

event: Indictment: the MLC halts royalty payments to Smith and confronts him; his representatives write 'Mike categorically denies any play manipulation' (Mar 17), 'Mike is the 'human' author!' (Mar 23), works 'not AI-generated' (Apr 27).
notes: Indictment ¶30 pp.14-15. MLC CEO Kris Ahrend (2024) and MLC (2026) say it withheld/prevented diversion of mechanical royalties.

event: Indictment alleges Smith emails that his music has 'generated at this point over 4 billion streams and $12 million in royalties since 2019.'
notes: Indictment ¶25 p.12. Smith's own claim as alleged - not a finding.

event: Sealed indictment (24 Cr. 504) returned: conspiracy to commit wire fraud, wire fraud, money-laundering conspiracy.
notes: Filed date per docket note in S006 row; indictment signed by U.S. Attorney Damian Williams.

event: Indictment unsealed; Smith (52) arrested Wednesday morning in Cornelius, NC (at his home outside Charlotte per RS) and to be presented before a U.S. magistrate judge in North Carolina; NY docket logs Rule 5(c)(3) documents from W.D.N.C. and an unsealing order by Magistrate Judge Valerie Figueredo; DOJ calls it the 'First Criminal Case Involving Artificially Inflated Music Streaming'; each count max 20 years.
notes: Williams: 'it's time for Smith to face the music.' Smith's attorney declined comment (S027); AP: lawyer did not return email (S046). Same day MLC CEO Kris Ahrend: MLC 'withheld payment of the associated mechanical royalties' (S027). Never show the street address.

event: Arraignment; bail set: $500,000 personal recognizance bond, two cosigners, travel limits, no contact with known co-conspirators (Judge Koeltl).
notes: Smith pleaded not guilty (reported S028).

event: UMG, Capitol, ABKCO and Concord sue Believe S.A. and TuneCore (S.D.N.Y. 24-cv-8406), seeking damages of 'at least $500,000,000'; Believe says it 'strongly refute[d]' the claims.
notes: Complaint ¶9 p.4. Demand - not a payment.

event: Denmark's Western High Court raises a streaming-fraud sentence (bots on 689 tracks) from 18 to 24 months.
notes: Comparator; different country and law.

event: Spotify restates that preventive measures limited Smith's Spotify royalties to ~$60,000; Pandora cites $1,500 exposure; SoundCloud declines a figure.
notes: Platform statements. Spotify's first version was 2024-09-12 (E044).

event: Spotify says it removed 'over 75 million spammy tracks' in the past 12 months and announces a music spam filter.
notes: Why-now context.

event: IFPI's Victoria Oakley and RIAA's Mitch Glazier publish 'End Streaming Fraud' op-ed: 'This is theft, plain and simple.'
notes: Industry position.

event: Smith waives indictment, is charged in a one-count Superseding Information (18 U.S.C. § 371, conspiracy to commit wire fraud) and pleads guilty before Judge Koeltl under a plea agreement; max 5 years.
notes: Key legal turn: plea to a new 5-year-max count instead of the 20-year counts.

event: Consent Preliminary Order of Forfeiture/Money Judgment: $8,091,843.64 money judgment = proceeds Smith personally obtained; Smith admits those proceeds 'cannot be located upon the exercise of due diligence'; final as to him and part of the sentence.
notes: Also ADMISSION of forfeiture allegation. Payment/collection status UNKNOWN.

event: U.S. Attorney Jay Clayton: 'Although the songs and listeners were fake, the millions of dollars Smith stole was real.' MLC says it 'prevented the diversion of mechanical royalties away from rightful songwriters'.
notes: Party statements.

event: UMG and Believe/TuneCore file a Joint Stipulation of Dismissal With Prejudice; financial terms undisclosed; UMG says resolved 'amicably'.
notes: Stipulation itself PACER-only (Dkt. 66 so-ordered 2026-04-08 per docket listing). No admission documented.

event: Deezer: ~75,000 AI tracks/day, ~44% of daily uploads; AI music 1-3% of streams; 85% of those streams fraudulent and demonetized.
notes: Deezer's own measurement on Deezer.

event: Judge Koeltl endorses defense letter: sentencing adjourned from July 29 to Tuesday, October 6, 2026, 3:00 pm; defense submissions due Sept 22; government submissions due late Sept (handwritten 28 or 29).
notes: Letter dated 2026-05-28 (government consented). Verify handwriting visually.

event: CVC Capital Partners announces majority investment in DistroKid (terms undisclosed; close expected Q3 2026); complaint cites a reported $2 billion valuation.
notes: Valuation is 'reported' (S001 ¶48).

event: Deezer: AI tracks exceed 50% of daily uploads at June 2026 peak (~90,000/day); will take down AI tracks used for fraud and those unstreamed for 6+ months.
notes: Deezer's own figures.

event: IFPI launches Streaming Integrity Initiative (KYC, content vetting incl. AI risk, intelligence sharing); UMG, Sony, Warner among signatories; DistroKid and TuneCore not on the list.
notes: List as published at launch.

event: UMG, Capitol Records and Capitol CMG sue DistroKid (D. Del. 1:26-cv-01156): Delaware DTPA + copyright + pre-1972 claims; jury demand.
notes: DistroKid: 'We strongly disagree with UMG's allegations...' (S005/S026).

event: Defense files sentencing memorandum (Dkt. 57, PACER-only) seeking probation; reportedly argues 'no individual artist or songwriter suffered any perceptible harm'; reported Guidelines 46-57 months, Probation recommends 24 months. Same day, letter (Dkt. 58) asks to seal unredacted memo and Exhibit A letters of support (non-party health info).
notes: Memo quotes are second-hand (Billboard via MBW/Music Ally). Dkt. 59 'Application Granted' (S011).

event: BET 'One Shot' announced with Smith as executive producer and main judge; Smith: 'the first nationally-televised competition specific to hip-hop'; $100,000 prize + recording contract; premiere August 2016.
notes: Backstory; Smith's own voice (C104).

event: Promoter Tony Mantor celebrates Smith's 12th week on the monitored adult-contemporary airplay charts; on monitored charts: 'They can't manipulate it.' (per Rolling Stone).
notes: Refines E003; irony beat (C102).

event: Jazz (Deluxe) by Smith and Hay reported at No. 1 on Billboard Jazz and Contemporary Jazz Albums; Smith on Instagram: 'I officially have a Number 1 Billboard Album!!!!'
notes: Exact week UNKNOWN. Not alleged to be fraudulent - never imply.

event: Smith posts Spotify stats on Instagram showing 214,875 monthly listeners: 'That's crazy and thanks to everyone who listens ... Truly grateful!' (per Rolling Stone).
notes: Original post not retrieved (Instagram); RS description only.

event: Spotify's first statement: its measures 'limited the royalties Smith was able to game from Spotify to approximately $60,000 of the $10,000,000 noted in the indictment.'
notes: Earliest platform statement.

event: Rolling Stone publishes long-form feature on Smith (pre-plea); trial then expected Oct. 6.
notes: Day not confirmed (~Jan 22 per social share).

event: Digital Music News: Apple Music, Boomplay, Tidal, YouTube and Amazon Music gave 'radio silence' when asked what they paid Smith.
notes: Who-paid open loop (C097).

event: SCHEDULED: Smith sentencing before Judge Koeltl, 3:00 pm. Also the reported answer deadline for DistroKid, LLC in the UMG suit.
notes: Future event as of 2026-09-26 - refresh before script lock. The two deadlines share a date by coincidence; never imply a link.
